einzeiler: Lance Bradley joins the show to discuss WSOP ratings and future broadcasts.
kurzfassung: Lance Bradley joins the podcast to analyze the TV ratings and reception of the WSOP's return to ESPN. The conversation covers the challenges of balancing nostalgic appeal with modern poker audiences and reflects on the breakout stars of the summer. Later, the host shares personal thoughts on missing the NAPT and live poker's overall health.
stichpunkte: Lance Bradley breaks down the TV ratings and overall reception of the WSOP on ESPN
Discussion on the difficulties of satisfying both casual viewers and hardcore poker fans
Reflecting on the standout winners, memorable stories, and new champions from the summer
Exploring the history and absence of online poker tracking leaderboards like PocketFives
The host shares thoughts on missing the North American Poker Tour in Las Vegas
Examining strong attendance numbers across various live poker tournaments worldwide
Breaking down the newly released schedule for the upcoming WSOP Paradise series in the Bahamas

clips.text: Two million people tuned in to watch a past final table winner on television nearly two decades ago.
Current audiences have grown to be ten to twelve times larger than the figures seen on previous cable broadcasts.
The early days relied on people sending emails to a few individuals in a dorm room to figure out top players.
An Illinois poker state championship drew over eighteen hundred entries to set a brand new record.
Managing morning drop-off and afternoon pick-up times right in the middle of the workday is extremely frustrating.
